text: Mr. Okoro wound the hall clock. “It runs slow again,” Mr. Okoro said. The smell of brass polish put him back in his uncle’s workshop.
Ilse heard the bell from the yard. Then the bell took her back to her first school, and to the smell of chalk dust.
Dana set the fern on the sill. Its green fronds gave her a quiet sense of calm. The radio in the next room barely reached her.
Every morning before the ferry left, Tomas checked the mooring lines. He no longer had to think about the knots.
Rosa saw the grey film on the jar and caught a sharp, sour smell. She knew the starter had turned.
The kiln cooled overnight. Ash lay in a grey ring on the shelf.
